mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class C43 AMG engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement M276 engine for a C43 AMG typically costs between £1,200 and £6,500 depending on condition. Used units start from £1,200-£2,500, reconditioned from £2,800-£4,500, and fully rebuilt from £3,200-£6,500. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 for AMG-specialist work.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz C-Class C43 AMG have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The C43 AMG uses the M276 engine, which has a timing chain, not a belt. However, the M276 is known for camshaft adjuster rattle and timing chain tensioner wear - a rattling noise on cold start (2-3 seconds) is the classic warning sign. Mercedes has a service bulletin (LI05.10-P-056435) on this for M276/M278 engines.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class C43 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs of engine problems in the C43 AMG include: a rattling noise on cold start (camshaft adjuster or timing chain tensioner), reduced power or intermittent limp mode (turbo/wastegate issues), a rattle from the turbocharger area (wastegate linkage wear), rough idle (PCV/oil separator issues), and grey smoke under hard acceleration. If you experience any of these, have the car inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class C43 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and mileage. A W205 C43 AMG is typically worth £12,000-£30,000 - a rebuilt M276 engine (£3,200-£6,500) is usually well within the car's value and can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. For lower-value examples or those with multiple issues, a specialist repair may be more economical than a full replacement.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M276 engine in the C43 AMG and the M177 in the C63 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M276 is a 3.0-litre V6 biturbo engine used in the C43 AMG, producing 367-390 hp. The M177 is a 4.0-litre V8 biturbo engine used in the C63 AMG, producing 476-510 hp. The M276 features a 60° V-angle and compact twin-turbo layout, while the M177 is a 90° V8 with 'hot-vee' turbo placement. Both are hand-built under AMG's 'One Man, One Engine' philosophy.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz C-Class C43 AMG to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the C43 AMG is most commonly caused by turbocharger and wastegate issues. The M276 biturbo can suffer from wastegate rattle, linkage wear and underboost complaints. A low-boost code does not automatically mean the turbocharger has failed - a vacuum leak, weak vacuum supply, leaking pneumatic actuator, sticking wastegate, worn linkage, faulty pressure transducer, boost leak or sensor issue can all produce a similar complaint. Other causes include camshaft adjuster failure affecting valve timing and HPFP issues affecting fuel delivery.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class C43 AMG - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C43 AMG badge arrived with the W205 generation in 2016, reviving the "43" designation last seen on the W202 C43 of the 1990s. Powered by the M276 3.0-litre V6 biturbo engine - a compact, responsive twin-turbo unit with a 60° V-angle - the C43 AMG was positioned as the entry-point to AMG performance, sitting below the V8-powered C63. It represented a significant shift from the naturally aspirated V8s of old, offering forced-induction performance with improved efficiency and everyday usability.

milestones.description: M276.823, 3.0L V6 biturbo, 367 hp (270 kW) - W205 C43 AMG launch; 520 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 4.7 seconds; 9G-TRONIC automatic; 4MATIC standard
M276.823, 3.0L V6 biturbo, 390 hp (287 kW) - W205 C43 AMG facelift; power increase to 390 hp; 0-62 mph improved to 4.5 seconds
W205 production ends; C43 AMG badge replaced by C43 AMG 4MATIC+ with M139 2.0L four-cylinder in new generation

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class C43 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The C43 AMG uses Mercedes' M276 3.0-litre V6 biturbo engine - a compact, responsive twin-turbo unit with a 60° V-angle and direct injection. While generally robust when properly maintained, it has predictable weak points. The M276 biturbo uses one turbocharger per cylinder bank, with each mounted close to the exhaust outlets to reduce exhaust energy loss and improve response. Rebuilt C43 AMG engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components designed to address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: M276 Camshaft Adjuster & Timing Chain Tensioner Rattle
problems.h4: M276 Camshaft Adjuster & Timing Chain Tensioner Rattle - Cold Start Noise in the C43 AMG
problems.rootCause: The M276 engine suffers from camshaft adjuster failure and timing chain tensioner wear. A rattling noise on cold start (2-3 seconds) is a common complaint on M276 engines. The M276 has secondary tensioner oil feed issues - when parked, the pressure/oil drains back out and causes it to rattle for a few seconds until oil pressure returns. Mercedes has a service bulletin (LI05.10-P-056435) on this for M276/M278 engines.

For vehicles under £15,000, a tensioner and check valve replacement (£700-£1,200) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. A £700-£1,200 specialist tensioner and check valve replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Once the camshaft adjusters fail, replacement costs approach rebuild territory.

problems.h4: M276 Biturbo Wastegate & Turbocharger Issues - Boost Loss and Reduced Power
problems.rootCause: The M276 biturbo engine can suffer from wastegate rattle, linkage wear and underboost complaints. The turbochargers and wastegate components live in a high-heat environment, which can cause the wastegate linkage to wear and the pneumatic actuators to fail. Common customer complaints include reduced power, intermittent limp mode, poor acceleration, delayed boost response, a check engine light, or a rattle from the turbocharger area. The system is designed to produce charge pressure of roughly 0.8 bar under operating conditions.

problems.recommendation: If your C43 AMG experiences reduced power or a rattle from the engine bay, have the turbocharger and wastegate system inspected. A low-boost code does not automatically mean the turbocharger has failed - a vacuum leak, weak vacuum supply, leaking pneumatic actuator, sticking wastegate, worn linkage, faulty pressure transducer, boost leak or sensor issue can all produce a similar complaint. A £500-£900 wastegate repair is significantly cheaper than a £2,000 turbo replacement.

problems.rootCause: The PCV system and oil separator can fail, causing rough idle, loss of performance, and increased oil consumption. The oil separator is a known weak point on the M276 engine.
